evals.prompt: I'm setting up a Cribl Stream Splunk LB destination with three indexers. idx-new is on beefier hardware so I gave it Load Weight 7, the other two (idx-a, idx-b) are weight 1 and 2. We forward about 300k events/sec total. How much traffic lands on each indexer?
evals.expected_output: idx-a 10% (30k events/sec), idx-b 20% (60k events/sec), idx-new 70% (210k events/sec); total weight 10

evals.prompt: We want our Cribl destination to send 25% of data to each of two old indexers and 50% to the new one. What Load Weight values should I configure?
evals.expected_output: Smallest integer weights 1, 1, 2 for old1, old2, new

evals.prompt: I set one of my Cribl receivers to Load Weight 0 and another to 5 — why is the first one getting nothing, and what split do I get if I change it to 0 vs 1 vs 5?
evals.expected_output: Explains weight 0 means Cribl opens no connections (valid drain technique); 0:5 = 0%/100%, 1:5 ≈ 16.67%/83.33%, 5:5 = 50%/50%
